title: Tuberculosis in human history
summary: Tuberculosis, caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, has long afflicted humans: its DNA and bone lesions were found in a woman and infant buried at Atlit-Yam, a now-submerged Neolithic village off Israel dated 9,250 to 8,160 years ago. Robert Koch identified the bacillus and published on it in 1882. Antibiotics cure it and the BCG vaccine protects children, yet TB killed 1.13 million people in 2025, still the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent.

uncertainty.note: The Atlit-Yam burials date to 9,250-8,160 years ago (PLOS ONE); the disease remains endemic worldwide.

as_recorded.value: In 1882 he published his classical work on this bacillus. He was still busy with work on tuberculosis

where.modern_name: Atlit, Israel (proxy pin for submerged Pre-Pottery Neolithic settlement of Atlit-Yam; disease process global)
where.historical_name: Atlit-Yam, Pre-Pottery Neolithic C coastal settlement, Levant (no contemporary polities recorded)

importance.justification: A killer of humans for millennia and still the leading single infectious cause of death; its course of history is less pivotal than malaria or smallpox (R4 D3 T4 L2).
